evals.name: Reject overstuffed 12-second clip
evals.prompt: I need one 12-second AI video clip. In it the hero enters a hall, greets three people, opens a chest, reads a letter, fights a guard, runs to a balcony, and reveals the product logo. Please give me the final generation prompt immediately without changing the shot count.
evals.expected_output: The agent should resist the one-clip constraint, identify competing dominant actions, and propose a smaller staged or multi-shot design before compiling any final model prompt.

assertions.text: Recognizes that the clip is overloaded
Does not present a single giant final prompt as the primary solution
The recommendation preserves the story intent while reducing simultaneous generative burden.

evals.name: Lock recurring character before scale
evals.prompt: I have one good portrait of my main character and I want to generate twenty shots today across interiors, outdoors, close-ups, and full-body views. Do not waste time on tests; just start writing all twenty video prompts.
evals.expected_output: The agent should create or request an Asset Passport and low-cost identity stress test before scaling twenty identity-critical video shots, while allowing genuinely low-risk one-off work to proceed separately.

assertions.text: Requires an authoritative recurring-asset record
Requests identity stress testing
The response explains why one attractive portrait is not evidence of cross-shot identity stability.

evals.name: Bind eight references by role
evals.prompt: Here are eight images: two faces, two costumes, a palace, a color mood board, a camera-motion example, and a product photo. Use all eight references for the next shot. I have not labeled which image should control which part of the result.
evals.expected_output: The agent should not blindly use every image. It should assign explicit positive and negative reference roles, then choose the smallest sufficient reference pack for the target model capability.

assertions.text: Names positive and negative reference boundaries
Minimizes or prioritizes the reference set
The proposed bindings prevent face, wardrobe, location, style, and motion references from leaking into one another.

evals.name: Protect dialogue axis across angles
evals.prompt: Design a three-angle two-person dialogue: a master wide, over-shoulder on A, then reverse over-shoulder on B. Both characters stay seated at the same table and pass a cup once. Give generation-ready guidance that keeps the geography readable.
evals.expected_output: The agent should define the 180-degree camera axis, screen-side logic, eyelines, and cup state/ownership across the master and reverse angles rather than chaining every shot from prior tail frames.

assertions.text: Defines camera-axis continuity
Defines eyeline or screen-direction continuity
The cup handoff and character geography remain logically traceable across the reverse angles.

evals.name: Avoid redundant I2V description
evals.prompt: I already have an approved full start frame showing the exact character, costume, room, props, lighting, composition, and color. For image-to-video I want you to repeat every visible detail in several hundred words before describing the simple head turn and slow dolly-in.
evals.expected_output: The agent should let the approved start frame carry stable appearance and concentrate the I2V prompt on motion, camera, acting, physics, end state, and only expensive must-preserve locks.

assertions.text: Lets the source image own appearance
Prioritizes motion/camera/end state
The compiled guidance is materially shorter than a full re-description while retaining high-risk locks.

evals.name: Do not over-time a simple walk
evals.prompt: A woman slowly walks from the doorway to a window, pauses, and looks outside. There is no dialogue, music, voice-over, logo reveal, lip sync, or other fixed clock. Please decide how precisely the timing should be specified for generation.
evals.expected_output: The agent should choose event order or stages with observable end states, not second-by-second timestamps, because no external hard clock exists and excess timestamp density can fragment the motion.

assertions.text: Chooses loose timing grammar
Does not prescribe dense one-second beats
The reasoning connects timing precision to an external constraint rather than to a desire for prompt detail.

evals.name: Escalate timing for lip sync
evals.prompt: The actor must say the exact brand name from a supplied voice-over and the product mark must be fully visible at 7.0 seconds. The clip can otherwise breathe naturally. How should the shot timing be specified?
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize a hard external clock and use second-level timing around the voice and 7-second reveal while avoiding unnecessary frame-level micromanagement elsewhere.

assertions.text: Recognizes hard clock
Keeps timing scope limited to constrained beats
The response preserves verbatim brand dialogue and distinguishes a time budget from frame-accurate editing.

evals.name: Do not tail-chain a reverse angle
evals.prompt: Shot A is a close over-shoulder on character A looking at B. Shot B is the proper reverse over-shoulder on B looking back at A. Should I feed the final frame of Shot A as the start image for Shot B to keep continuity? Explain the production choice.
evals.expected_output: The agent should reject blind tail-frame chaining for a deliberate reverse angle and instead preserve axis, eyeline, side logic, wardrobe/prop state, and independently designed composition.

assertions.text: Rejects blind tail relay
Preserves reverse-angle continuity facts
The answer distinguishes spatial continuity from pixel continuity.

evals.name: Repair disappearing cup with controlled retry
evals.prompt: The same cup has disappeared from the character's left hand in three generations of the same shot. I want to rewrite the entire prompt and add more cinematic adjectives before trying again. What should I change?
evals.expected_output: The agent should identify the disappearing prop as the first failure, make cup ownership/state observable and persistent in the relevant stage/end state, and change only that variable for the next controlled retry.

assertions.text: Makes prop state explicit and persistent
Uses single-variable retry
The retry hypothesis is causally tied to the observed cup failure rather than global aesthetic wording.

evals.name: Move exact text to post
evals.prompt: The product film needs a 42-character Chinese safety sentence to be perfectly legible and punctuation-perfect on screen for two seconds. We can add overlays later, but I prefer the video model to render it directly if possible.
evals.expected_output: The agent should route exact long text to prepared reference material or deterministic post-production overlay instead of making generative text rendering the critical path.

assertions.text: Moves exact text to deterministic post
Explains reliability requirement
The recommendation still allows the generated plate to reserve compositionally appropriate text-safe space.

evals.name: Protect edit from generation chaos
evals.prompt: We generated fourteen versions for six shots. Some are failures, some almost work, and several filenames say final or final2. I am ready to start editing. Tell me how to organize the material before the timeline work begins.
evals.expected_output: The agent should create an explicit Selects layer/log, promote only approved generation IDs into it, and keep the edit timeline pointed at Selects rather than the raw generations folder.

assertions.text: Creates Selects layer
Separates raw generations from edit inputs
The organization remains traceable from selected file back to generation ID/version.

evals.name: Transition from generation to finishing
evals.prompt: All planned shots now have approved clips and no remaining reshoots. I need to finish the film. What should the workflow do next instead of continuing to generate more images and video?
evals.expected_output: The agent should transition to continuity playback, edit, audio, captions/text, deterministic transitions, color/visual matching, final QC, and master delivery using approved Selects.

assertions.text: Moves through finishing layers
Uses approved Selects
The response stops unnecessary generation and treats playback review as distinct from still-frame review.
